annotation.title_clean: Report from the Commission to the European Parliament and the Council: Report adopted pursuant to Article 112(1) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 on the need to review the list of prohibited AI practices and of high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III
annotation.title_en: Report from the Commission to the European Parliament and the Council: Report adopted pursuant to Article 112(1) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 on the need to review the list of prohibited AI practices and of high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III
named_instruments_referenced: Regulation on Transparency and Targeting of Political Advertising
Charter of Fundamental Rights of the EU
annotation.summary_en: First annual European Commission report under Article 112(1) of the AI Act. Drawing on Member State input, a stakeholder consultation and OECD incident data, it concludes there is no immediate need to amend Article 5 prohibitions or Annex III high-risk use cases. It flags a possible gap on AI-generated CSAM and non-consensual intimate deepfakes, plus several areas for further monitoring.
key_provisions_or_claims: Member States and most stakeholders see no current need to amend Article 5 or Annex III given limited implementation experience
Potential regulatory gap identified: AI systems generating CSAM and non-consensual sexually explicit deepfakes are not covered by Article 5
AI companions, mental-health chatbots, emotion recognition, dark patterns, debt collection and critical infrastructure AI flagged for monitoring
Analysis of 3,791 OECD AIM incidents: about 10% relate to Annex I products (e.g., medical devices, self-driving vehicles)
AI Office to coordinate monitoring with AI Board and national authorities ahead of the next annual review
